Erroneous

/ih-ROH-nee-uhs/ - the stress falls on ROH · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Erroneous means containing error; factually incorrect.

The museum quietly corrected an erroneous caption that had the explorer sailing for the wrong king.

Worked Example

For a week the airline blamed the fog. Then a scheduler noticed the real culprit: one erroneous entry in the crew database had Captain Weiss down as having left the airline, so the system had been grounding her flights while she sat, fully certified, in the pilots' lounge. One wrong field, four hundred stranded passengers, and not a cloud to blame.

Erroneous is the exact word for that database entry: containing error, factually incorrect. The word passes no judgment on how the mistake got there — no lie is implied, no carelessness proven. It simply stamps the entry false. That even-handedness is why reports, captions, and beliefs get called erroneous, while the people who hold them are merely mistaken.

How Erroneous Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

incorrect

incorrect: plainly not right; erroneous adds a formal, official flavor

inaccurate

inaccurate: off the true value, perhaps only slightly

Antonyms

accurate

accurate: matching the facts exactly

correct

correct: right, with nothing to fix

How Strong Is It? — imprecise → erroneous → preposterous

imprecise vs. erroneous

imprecise vs. erroneous: An imprecise figure is loose but circles the truth; an erroneous one has left the truth entirely.

preposterous vs. erroneous

preposterous vs. erroneous: Preposterous goes past erroneous — wrong so loudly that no one needs a fact-checker to see it.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — erron

Root — erron: a wanderer (Latin errare, to wander, to stray)

Suffix — -eous

Suffix — -eous: of the nature of

Put it together

Put it together: Erron- (a wanderer, from Latin errare, "to wander, to stray") + -eous (of the nature of) = of the nature of straying. To the Romans an erro was a drifter who had left the road; an erroneous figure has done the same — wandered off the path of fact. Err, error, and errant all walk the same root.

Use the root in a new word: errant

Use the root in a new word: errant: An errant tee shot cleared two fairways and a snack cart before landing.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / on the record

Erroneous is the formal stamp for entries, figures, reports, and beliefs that are factually incorrect — the auditor's and editor's word. People are mistaken, never erroneous. Note the line between it and this unit's simplistic: a simplistic account may be accurate as far as it goes, just thinner than the truth; an erroneous one states what is false.
